OpenSASE is an open, self-hosted SASE-style edge, deployed from one source of truth: a Nix flake. Clients connect over OpenVPN; an mitmproxy addon decrypts and re-encrypts traffic per a URL-category policy; every payload is scanned by ClamAV; every verdict — `splice`, `bump`, `clean`, `INFECTED` — is written to a JSONL decision log.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    client["VPN client"] --> vpn["openvpn udp/5443"]
    vpn --> mitm["mitmproxy<br/>splice | bump per URL category"]
    mitm --> clam["clamd :3310"]
    mitm --> log[("decisions.jsonl")]
    mitm --> net((Internet))
```

It is growing two halves: the **SASE edge** for teams and servers, and a **home appliance** — install it like a Pi-hole and every family device routes through it, with per-device policy, traffic visibility, and verdicts. The stack stays modular: the bare-minimum decrypt edge stands alone; scanner, DNS-policy, agent-inspection, and chat modules layer on as opt-ins. The planned shapes live in [Future](docs/future.qmd); the working tracker is the [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.qmd).

Two deployment paths:

::: { layout-ncol="2" }
### Containers — no Nix required

Pre-built OCI images are published to GHCR by CI. Pull and `docker compose up` on Linux, macOS, or Windows, any OCI runtime.

[Deploy with Docker →](docs/deployment.qmd)

### NixOS appliance

The same stack as stock NixOS modules: build a QEMU VM, `nixos-rebuild` a physical machine, or deploy remotely with `--target-host`.

[Deploy with Nix →](docs/deployment.qmd)
:::

### Kubernetes

Prebuilt manifests are not shipped yet (a kustomize follow-up is tracked). The four images are stateless OCI and stage on Kubernetes with the standard contract — `NET_ADMIN` on `openvpn`, `RWO` volumes per service, PKI injected before the VPN starts. See the [README Kubernetes section](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase#kubernetes) for the staging table and constraints.

## Purely declarative

Every deployable artifact is derived, not hand-maintained. There is no `docker build` anywhere in the repo's release path — the same flake that boots the appliance emits the containers, so what you run as a container is exactly what NixOS would run, byte-for-byte.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    flake["flake.nix<br/>single source of truth"] --> imgs["nix/images.nix<br/>dockerTools.buildLayeredImage"]
    flake --> appl["nix/appliance.nix<br/>NixOS module"]
    flake --> cue["k8s/manifests.cue"]
    imgs --> ghcr["ghcr.io/shsingh/opensase-*<br/>(:latest + version)"]
    appl --> ghcr
    cue --> manifests["k8s/manifests.yaml<br/>(cue export, committed)"]
    imgs --> compose["docker-compose.yml"]
```

**One flake, four surfaces.** The flake is the only place versions, image references, ports, capabilities, and volume paths are declared; everything else consumes it:

- **OCI containers without Dockerfiles.** Each service is a `pkgs.dockerTools.buildLayeredImage` derivation (`nix/images.nix`): the store path for the binary, a minimal closure, the few files a bare image lacks (`/etc/passwd`, CA certs, `/tmp`). Because images are hashes of inputs rather than layers of imperative `RUN` statements, CI and a local `nix run .#load-images` produce byte-identical images — nothing floats, no base image is ever pulled at release time.
- **The appliance is modules, not scripts.** `nix/appliance.nix` composes stock NixOS services — `services.openvpn`, `services.dnsmasq`, `services.clamav`, plus `services.opensase` (the mitmproxy addon + decision log) — so the appliance is defined, not assembled, and every knob is a typed NixOS option checkable by `nix flake check`.
- **Kubernetes manifests as CUE.** The same service model (images, ports, capabilities, volumes) is expressed once in `k8s/manifests.cue` with a typed schema; `nix run .#k8s-manifests` (`cue export ./k8s -e list`) renders the committed `k8s/manifests.yaml`. CUE was chosen over hand-written YAML or Helm because the constraints live next to the data: a service that needs `NET_ADMIN` must declare it in type, so compose, the appliance, and Kubernetes cannot drift apart.
- **PKI in the flake too.** CA bootstrap and per-device client profiles come from flake apps (`vpn-init`, `vpn-getclient`) that vendor easyRSA via Nix — no `curl | bash`, no drifting helper scripts.

The payoff is uniformity: one lockfile determines the appliance boot, the GHCR images, the compose wiring, and the Kubernetes base manifests. Consumers who never touch Nix still benefit — they pull `dockerTools`-produced images whose every layer is hash-pinned to the same nixpkgs revision CI used.
